newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain sees no change in French attitude to Europe.
newsitem.headline: Spain sees no change in French attitude to Europe.

text.p: Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said on Monday he did not expect a left-wing victory in French elections to significantly affect efforts to forge a more united Europe.
"I don't suppose there will be any change in the big decisions on the construction of Europe," Matutes told Spanish reporters in Luxembourg where he was attending a meeting of EU foreign ministers.
Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja earlier urged the new French government to maintain close cooperation in combatting terrorism.
"The anti-terrorist battle must be and is separate from ideologies and from partisan debates of left and right," Mayor Oreja told reporters.
He added he was confident the "exemplary" cooperation between centre-right governments in France and Spain before the election would continue under a Socialist-led coalition.

Spain's year-old conservative government has repeatedly expressed its satisfaction with a tougher French attitude towards Basque separatist guerrilla group ETA over the past year. ETA has a strong power base in southern France.
Spain's opposition Socialist and Communist parties welcomed the election outcome.
The Socialists said a policy of "neoliberalism" in recent years had created uncertainty about European integration and prompted a turn toward socialism and social democracy in France and Britain.
"If they had elections in Germany, the Social Democrats would probably win too," said Socialist secretary for international relations Raimon Obiols.
Obiols said the victory showed the need for Europe to confront the problems of unemployment and social fractures.
The Communist-led United Left (IU) coalition said it hoped the new government would deal with more than social issues.
"(The election result) is magnificent news for all of the European left," said IU for international relations spokesman Carlos Carnero.

Both government and opposition figures called for the new French government to put a speedy end to attacks on Spanish trucker importing fruits and vegetables by French farmers demanding tighter control on cheaper imported produce.
